name: Security deposit too high
what_to_look_for: A security deposit larger than two months' rent in the first year of the lease, or larger than one month's rent at the start of the second year or later.
why_it_matters: Pennsylvania law caps the deposit at two months' rent in the first year and one month's rent from the second year on.
question_to_ask: Can you confirm the deposit amount? I understand PA law limits it to two months' rent in the first year.
source_name: PA Landlord and Tenant Act of 1951, 68 P.S. 250.511a

name: Deposit return too slow or not itemized
what_to_look_for: Language letting the landlord return the deposit later than 30 days after move-out, or keep it without giving a written itemized list of deductions.
why_it_matters: In Pennsylvania the landlord must return the deposit, with an itemized list of any deductions, within 30 days after the tenant moves out.
question_to_ask: Will you return the deposit within 30 days with an itemized list of any deductions?
source_name: PA Landlord and Tenant Act of 1951, 68 P.S. 250.512

name: Non-refundable deposit or fee
what_to_look_for: Any part of the security deposit labeled non-refundable, or move-in, cleaning, or 'administrative' fees that cannot be returned.
why_it_matters: A deposit can only be kept for damage, unpaid rent, or lease breach. A 'non-refundable deposit' can be a way to keep money the law says should come back.
question_to_ask: What exactly is this fee for, and is any of it refundable?
source_name: Inquirer tenants' rights guide: security deposits

name: Tenant pays for all repairs
what_to_look_for: Clauses making the tenant responsible for all repairs, including major systems such as heat, plumbing, electrical, roof, or structure, or waiving the landlord's duty to keep the unit livable.
why_it_matters: Landlords have a duty to keep a rental safe and livable (the warranty of habitability). Tenants generally cannot sign that duty away.
question_to_ask: Who handles repairs to heat, plumbing, and electrical, and how do I request them?
source_name: Penn Off-Campus Services summary of Philadelphia tenant rights

name: Landlord not responsible for anything
what_to_look_for: Clauses saying the landlord is not liable for any injury, damage, or loss, even if caused by the landlord's own negligence.
why_it_matters: Broad liability waivers may not hold up, but they can discourage tenants from asserting their rights. Worth asking about before signing.
question_to_ask: If something breaks because of a building problem and damages my things, who is responsible?

name: Entry without notice
what_to_look_for: Language letting the landlord enter the unit at any time, for any reason, without advance notice.
why_it_matters: Your privacy depends on what the lease says. Ask for reasonable advance notice (for example, 24 hours) except in emergencies.
question_to_ask: Can we agree you'll give 24 hours' notice before entering, except in emergencies?

name: Waiver of notice or confession of judgment
what_to_look_for: Clauses where the tenant waives the right to notice before eviction, waives the right to go to court, or 'confesses judgment' (agrees in advance that the landlord wins any lawsuit).
why_it_matters: These clauses can take away key protections. Get the lease reviewed before signing anything like this.
question_to_ask: Can this waiver clause be removed?
source_name: Temple Law students' Landlord-Tenant Help Service (get a review)

name: High or stacking late fees
what_to_look_for: Late fees that are large compared to rent, that grow every day without a cap, or that start with no grace period.
why_it_matters: Daily late fees with no cap can grow quickly. Know the exact amount, the grace period, and the maximum.
question_to_ask: Is there a grace period, and what's the maximum late fee?

name: Automatic renewal
what_to_look_for: The lease renews automatically unless the tenant gives notice long in advance (for example, 60 or 90 days or more).
why_it_matters: Students who miss the notice deadline can get locked into another year or penalty fees.
question_to_ask: When exactly do I need to tell you if I'm not renewing, and how?

name: Rent can change mid-lease
what_to_look_for: Language letting the landlord raise rent or add new fees during the lease term.
why_it_matters: A fixed-term lease should lock in your rent. Mid-lease increases make budgeting impossible.
question_to_ask: Is the rent fixed for the whole lease term?
source_name: Penn Off-Campus Services summary of Philadelphia tenant rights

name: Tenant pays landlord's legal fees
what_to_look_for: The tenant must pay the landlord's attorney fees or court costs in any dispute, with no matching right for the tenant.
why_it_matters: One-sided fee clauses make it risky to dispute anything, even when you're right.
question_to_ask: Can the attorney-fee clause apply to both sides equally?

name: Joint and several liability
what_to_look_for: Roommates are 'jointly and severally' liable for the full rent and any damage.
why_it_matters: This is common and usually legal, but it means you can owe the whole rent if a roommate doesn't pay. Students should understand it before signing.
question_to_ask: If a roommate leaves, how is their share of rent handled?
